latest_release.body:
Prisma ORM 7.10.1 is a patch release. It fixes a bug where a nested interactive transaction could make later, unrelated transactions run inside the wrong transaction. It also updates dependencies that had security advisories.

## Fixes

### Prisma Client: nested `$transaction` no longer changes the options object you pass in

If you passed the same options object to a nested `tx.$transaction(...)` and later to a top-level `prisma.$transaction(...)`, the nested call wrote the outer transaction's id into that object. Every later top-level transaction that used the object was then treated as nested inside that old transaction:

- if the old transaction had committed, the new one failed with `P2028`;
- if the old transaction was still open, the new one silently ran as a savepoint inside another request's transaction.

```ts
const TX_OPTIONS = { timeout: 30_000, maxWait: 10_000 }

await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  await tx.$transaction(async (inner) => { /* ... */ }, TX_OPTIONS)
})

// Before 7.10.1, this call could fail with P2028 or join another transaction.
await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { /* ... */ }, TX_OPTIONS)
```

Prisma Client no longer modifies the options object. (https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30368, thanks @lazerg)

### Prisma Migrate: refuse a shadow database that is the main database

Prisma Migrate now refuses to run with error `P3025` when the shadow database URL points at the same database as the main database URL. Before, `prisma migrate diff --from-migrations` with that setup dropped the real schema, rebuilt it from the migrations, and reported an empty diff. (https://github.com/prisma/prisma-engines/pull/5851)

### MariaDB adapter: updated to `mariadb` 3.5.4

`@prisma/adapter-mariadb` now depends on `mariadb` 3.5.4, which fixes several security advisories in 3.5.3. The adapter no longer rewrites IPv6 hosts in connection strings, because `mariadb` 3.5.4 accepts them as written. IPv6 connection strings keep working without changes. (https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30668)

## Dependency updates

Dependencies with security advisories were updated: `mysql2`, `fast-uri`, `deepmerge-ts`, `mariadb` and `source-map-js`. (https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30314, https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30189, https://github.com/prisma/orm/pull/30668)

Docs | Discord | X | Blog Post | Architecture

--- > **Using Prisma 7?** It is maintained for eighteen months after `8.0.0` final; [supported versions](./docs/oss/versioning.md#supported-versions) says what that covers. Its source lives on the [`v7` branch](https://github.com/prisma/orm/tree/v7) of this repository and its docs at [prisma.io/docs/orm/v7](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7). > **Prisma 8 is a release candidate.** `8.0.0` final is expected in the next four to eight weeks. Until then a release candidate may include breaking changes, and every release ships with an upgrade recipe that the `prisma-8` skill applies for you. The candidate is a complete implementation we stand behind: we treat bugs in it as urgent, and the risk you take on is a feature that is not built yet rather than churn. The [feature scoreboard](./scorecard.md) names every gap. New projects should start here. Existing Prisma 7 applications can migrate incrementally, and Prisma 7 stays maintained on the [`v7` branch](https://github.com/prisma/orm/tree/v7) for eighteen months after `8.0.0` final. Star the repo, follow [@prisma on X](https://pris.ly/x), or read along on the [Prisma blog](https://www.prisma.io/blog). **Prisma 8** is a TypeScript rewrite of Prisma ORM, designed to be **extensible**, **composable**, and **AI-agent friendly** by default. Read the [announcement](https://pris.ly/pn-announcement) or start with the [docs](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm). ## Prerequisites - Node.js 24 or newer - A package manager (`npm`, `pnpm`, or `yarn`) ## Getting started ### 1. Scaffold a new project The interactive scaffolder picks an app template (Next.js, Hono, Nuxt, Astro, NestJS, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, or Elysia) and wires Prisma 8 in with your chosen database (PostgreSQL or MongoDB): ```bash npm create prisma ``` You finish with a runnable app, a starter contract, and the agent skills already installed.
